**Direct answer:** The main UN Headquarters complex in New York was completed in **October 1952**. The exact day is uncertain: sources give October 9 or October 10, 1952. October 10, 1952 is the date the article text uses. I could not find a primary source that settles which of the two is right.

**Claims and sources**

- Wikipedia's article text says the headquarters "was declared complete on October 10, 1952."
  https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Headquarters_of_the_United_Nations

- The infobox of that same Wikipedia article lists October 9, 1952, so the page disagrees with itself by one day.
  https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Headquarters_of_the_United_Nations

- The UN's own site says construction was completed in 1952, without a specific day (as summarized by the search tool; I did not open the page).
  https://www.un.org/ungifts/united-nations-ny-site

- The Secretariat Building was finished earlier, in June 1951, so it isn't the completion date of the whole complex (search summary, not verified by opening the page).
  https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Nations_Secretariat_Building

- Later additions came after 1952. The Dag Hammarskjöld Library was dedicated in November 1961, and a cafeteria and Conference Building expansion followed in 1978–1981.
  https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Headquarters_of_the_United_Nations

- Sources also disagree on when construction started. One gives a groundbreaking of September 14, 1948 and another gives UN Day, October 24, 1949 (search summary, not verified on the pages).
  https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Headquarters_of_the_United_Nations
  https://www.un.org/ungifts/united-nations-ny-site

I read only the first 100,000 of about 270,000 characters of the Wikipedia page. I did not check the Secretariat page or the UN page directly.
